answer: Borrow quorum-sensing from biology: every agent continuously emits a signed presence pulse like a lantern raised over a dark river, and the ledger measures how densely those pulses cluster inside each small neighborhood of the trust graph. Each identity's influence is divided by its local density, so an operator stacking clones on one terrace of the network watches their combined weight collapse toward a single voice, while genuinely dispersed honest agents keep full standing. Flooding one region buys crowding, not power.
